# Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0506a)

**ID:** Atk S0506a
**Section:** Aṭṭhakathā Khuddakanikāya (atk-s05)
**Collection:** Atthakatha-Suttas
**Title (Pali):** Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā
**Title (English, from literature):** Elucidation of the Intrinsic Meaning: The Commentary on the Vimāna Stories
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, known formally as the third part of the *Paramatthadīpanī*, is the commentary on the canonical *Vimānavatthu* of the Khuddakanikāya [Harvey 2012; Phaengcharoen 2006]. The commentary is ascribed to the South Indian commentator Dhammapāla (Dhammapālācariya) of Badaratitthavihāra [Chandawimala; Monius 2001]. Its narrative accounts regularly follow a recurring pattern: a protagonist (frequently a woman) performs an act of merit, devotion, or kindness toward the Buddha or the Saṅgha, is reborn in a heavenly realm such as Tāvatiṃsa, and is later questioned by a senior disciple concerning the deeds leading to her celestial splendor [Monius 2001]. Doctrinally, the commentary discusses the bodily brilliance and rays of the Buddha (*ketumālā*) and defines the physical marks of a Great Man as the "marks of a hundred merits" (*satapuññalakkhana*) produced through countless meritorious acts [Endo 1997]. It also incorporates non-Mahāvihāra traditions, including the Abhayagiri interpretation of the eight inopportune states of rebirth (*aṭṭhakkhaṇā*) [Chandawimala].

Within commentarial historiography, the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* is situated chronologically after the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* and prior to the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* [Goonesekere 1967]. Narrative details sometimes diverge from parallel accounts in the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā*, such as differing motivations attributed to the father when removing the dying youth Maṭṭakuṇḍalī outside his home [Adikaram 1946]. The Pali text was edited by E. Hardy for the Pali Text Society [Monius 2001; Phaengcharoen 2006] and was also printed in the Sinhalese Simon Hewavitarne Bequest series [Adikaram 1946]. An English translation by Peter Masefield, assisted by N. A. Jayawickrama, was published under the title *Elucidation of the Intrinsic Meaning So Named: The Commentary on the Vimāna Stories* [Monius 2001; Neelis 2010].

DharmaNexus identifies 37,539 text-reuse matches between the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* and 478 other Pali texts, with no cross-language matches scoring 10 or higher [DharmaNexus]. Its most extensive commentarial reuse is shared with its sister commentary, the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (over 2,300 matches and 184,000 shared characters; e.g., §3996–4016 ↔ §3216–3235), followed by the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā*, *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā*, *Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā*, *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, and *Udāna-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. In addition to these commentarial parallels, the work incorporates the canonical verses and prose of individual *Vimānavatthu* texts, including large reuse segments with the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Paṭhamanāvāvimānavatthu* (Vv 6), *Dutiyanāvāvimānavatthu* (Vv 7), *Sunikkhittavimānavatthu* (Vv 85), and *Tiladakkhiṇavimānavatthu* (Vv 10) [DharmaNexus].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0507a) (§3996–4016 ↔ §3216–3235); Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0502a) (§574_2–581_14 ↔ §3240_1–3248_2); Guttilavimānavatthu (Vv 33) (§1347_14–1371 ↔ §2.4–10.4); Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā (Paṭhamo bhāgo) (Atk S0508a1) (§3709_0–3709_8 ↔ §1125_6–1125_14); Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0510a) (§29_1–32_0 ↔ §930_3–933); Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0505a) (§2024_1–2024_7 ↔ §1064_1–1064_6); Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Dutiyo bhāgo) (Atk S0513a2) (§517_4–526 ↔ §1638_14–1644); Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā (Dutiyo bhāgo) (Atk S0508a2) (§2774_0–2774_2 ↔ §6503_2–6503_4)
- [Adikaram 1946] E. W. Adikaram, Early History of Buddhism in Ceylon (1946) — Discusses fifth-century commentary context, Maṭṭakuṇḍalī story divergence with Dhammapadaṭṭhakathā, and Hewavitarana edition.
- [Chandawimala] Rangama Chandawimala Thero, Impact of the Abhayagiri Practices on Development of Theravada Buddhism in Sri Lanka — Identifies authorship by Dhammapālācariya of Badaratitthavihāra and adoption of the Abhayagiri view of the eight inopportune rebirths (aṭṭhakkhaṇā).
- [DharmaNexus] DharmaNexus database — Supplied internal Pali text reuse statistics, major commentarial partners, and reuse with canonical Vimānavatthu suttas.
- [Endo 1997] Toshiichi Endo, Buddha in Theravada Buddhism: A Study of the Concept of Buddha in the Pali Commentaries (1997) — Details doctrinal definitions regarding ketumālā and satapuññalakkhana.
- [Goonesekere 1967] L. R. Goonesekere, Buddhist Commentarial Literature (1967) — Outlines relative chronology placing the text after Dhammapadaṭṭhakathā and before Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā.
- [Harvey 2012] Peter Harvey, An Introduction to Buddhism: Teachings, History and Practices (2nd ed., 2012) — Identifies text as Paramatthadīpanī III, commentary on Vv.
- [Monius 2001] Anne E. Monius, Imagining a Place for Buddhism: Literary Culture and Religious Community in Tamil-Speaking South India (2001) — Discusses narrative formulas of female rebirths, Dhammapāla's authorship, PTS edition by E. Hardy, and translation by Peter Masefield.
- [Neelis 2010] Jason Neelis, Early Buddhist Transmission and Trade Networks — Provides bibliographic details on Peter Masefield and N. A. Jayawickrama's translation.
- [Phaengcharoen 2006] Phramaha Somphong Santacitto Phaengcharoen, Analytical Study of Concept of Dhamma as Natural Law in Theravada (2006) — Cites Paramatthadīpanī III (Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā), edited by E. Hardy.
